goals: Mechanistic: quantify how initial water-table depth controls the fraction of a surface infiltration pulse that reaches the saturated zone (recharge) versus being stored/evaporated/drained in the unsaturated column
Secondary: characterize the LAG between the surface pulse and the water-table response as a function of initial WTD
key_processes: recharge to the aquifer store (QDRAI / aquifer recharge)
partitioning of infiltrated water between recharge, ET, and drainage

model_choice.rationale: Single-column 1-D ELM directly represents per-layer soil moisture, an aquifer store, and recharge — the ideal testbed for an idealized WTD-vs-recharge sensitivity with everything but initial WTD held fixed.

answerable: WTD control on pulse-to-recharge fraction for the SHALLOW-to-intermediate range (~0.5 m to ~28.8 m), the ELM aquifer range
lag / timing of water-table response as a function of initial WTD within that range
monotonicity and approximate shape of the recharge-fraction vs WTD relationship

not_answerable.aspect: WTD levels deeper than ~28.8 m (i.e. the 30-50 m end of the requested range)
not_answerable.why: ELM's aquifer range is 0.05-28.8 m; the WTD-informed warm start clamps deeper targets and pins the aquifer empty, so all deep levels collapse to the same clamped state and cannot be distinguished
not_answerable.needs: extended/deep aquifer representation in ELM (or an alternative deep vadose-zone model)

not_answerable.aspect: a clean, prescribed unit infiltration pulse at the top boundary
not_answerable.why: the runs can only pull forcing PERIOD, not inject a synthetic top-boundary water flux; the pulse must be approximated by a selected real precipitation event

sampling_strategy.approach: controlled / not spatial — single-factor idealized sweep on initial water-table depth
sampling_strategy.n_justification: Seven log-spaced WTD levels span shallow (near-saturated, pulse->recharge expected ~1) to the deepest depth ELM can represent (~28.8 m); log spacing resolves the expected nonlinear roll-off in recharge fraction with fewer runs than linear spacing. The requested 30-50 m levels are omitted as infeasible (see feasibility).
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Not spatial. One representative CONUS single-column location so that NLDAS-2 forcing is available and a discrete wet event can be selected; all columns share this location and forcing.
sampling_strategy.replication: None in the baseline (deterministic idealized sweep). Optional second uniform soil texture (sand vs clay) could be added later to test texture-dependence of the WTD effect; excluded here to keep the single-factor design clean.

sampling_plan.reason: near-saturated column: expected upper bound where nearly all of the pulse reaches the water table with minimal lag
resolves the high-recharge-fraction regime just below the root zone
mid-range level to resolve the nonlinear roll-off of recharge fraction
thick vadose zone: strong attenuation and lengthening lag expected
approaches the regime where little of a single pulse reaches the table within the event window

sampling_plan.group: deepest representable WTD (28.8 m, ELM clamp)
sampling_plan.reason: lower bound of resolvable response; marks the edge of ELM's aquifer range beyond which levels cannot be distinguished

validation_design.target_variable: pulse-to-recharge fraction (aquifer recharge / infiltrated pulse) and water-table response lag
validation_design.observation_source: physical expectation / vadose-zone theory (monotonic decline of recharge fraction and increasing lag with WTD); no in-domain observations exist for an idealized column
validation_design.comparison: analog — qualitative/quantitative consistency check against expected monotonic, saturating behavior rather than co-located data
validation_design.metric: monotonicity of recharge-fraction vs WTD; magnitude and sign of lag trend; internal water-balance closure
validation_design.n_validation_points: 0 (conceptual — validated against physical expectation, not data)

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: uniform synthetic soil (single texture, e.g. loam), single representative CONUS location, identical selected wet-event forcing, WTD-informed warm start to each target depth; only initial WTD varies

requires_capabilities.why: initial WTD IS the treatment; each column must be initialized to its target water table via the Fan-2013 warm start (one carrier run each)
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire experiment — without it columns cold-start at default ~8.8 m and the factor is not set

requires_capabilities.why: the requested 30-50 m range exceeds ELM's aquifer range and is clamped
requires_capabilities.blocks: the deep half of the requested WTD sweep

requires_capabilities.why: the runs cannot inject a controlled water flux; the pulse must be approximated by a selected real event
requires_capabilities.blocks: a clean unit-impulse interpretation of pulse-to-recharge fraction

requires_capabilities.capability: recharge / aquifer-flux diagnostic tracking (per-event recharge accounting)
requires_capabilities.why: need to isolate the fraction of the specific infiltration pulse reaching the water table and its timing
requires_capabilities.blocks: quantitative pulse-to-recharge partitioning and lag estimation

requires_capabilities.why: recharge and water table are slow states; short warm-started runs plus adequate settle time are needed before/after the pulse

assumptions: A single uniform synthetic soil texture (e.g. loam) is used so the response reflects WTD alone; texture sensitivity is out of scope for the baseline.
The infiltration pulse is approximated by a discrete wet precipitation event selected from 1980-2018 NLDAS-2 forcing, applied identically to all columns.
Root-zone soil moisture (a fast state) is left at default by the warm start and is assumed to have secondary influence relative to WTD; this is a known caveat, not a controlled variable.
ELM's 1-D equilibrium differs from Fan's lateral-flow equilibrium, so some drift from the target initial WTD is expected and is itself part of the recorded result.
A single representative CONUS location adequately supplies forcing; the location choice is not itself a driver.
open_questions: Should the deep end (>28.8 m) be pursued with an alternative deep-vadose-zone model, or is capping at the ELM aquifer range acceptable for the study's intent?
Is a natural selected wet event acceptable as the 'pulse', or is a truly prescribed synthetic impulse required (which needs a new forcing capability)?
Should a second soil texture be added to test whether the WTD control is texture-dependent?
What post-pulse window defines 'reaches the water table' — days, weeks, or full seasonal recharge?
